title: Checking the Time on a Poster

source.rights: 原创 AI 辅助虚构教学材料，尚待发布前独立审核。

questions.prompt: What time did Paul mean for the conversation?
questions.evidence: I meant two in the afternoon.
questions.explanation: Paul 原本的意思是下午两点，而不是上午十点。

questions.prompt: What information is missing from the poster?
questions.evidence: The poster says “Saturday” but does not mention a time.
questions.explanation: 海报写了周六，却没有时间。

questions.prompt: Who will check whether the hall is free?
questions.evidence:
Could you tell me whether the hall is free at two? I have not received a response from the manager yet.
Iris: I can ask her now.
questions.explanation: Paul 请 Iris 核实，Iris 回应自己现在可以询问经理。

questions.prompt: What does Iris say is their purpose?
options: To give people the right information.
answers: To give people the right information.
questions.evidence: Our purpose is to make sure people have the right information, not to blame anyone.
questions.explanation: 她说明目的在于确保信息正确，而非指责。

questions.prompt: When does the manager ask for a reminder?
questions.evidence: She asks us to remind her on Friday.
questions.explanation: 经理请他们在周五提醒。

questions.evidence: The side door. The main door is being repaired.
questions.explanation: 主门正在维修，因此应走侧门。

questions.prompt: What additional information can go on the poster?
questions.evidence: We can also include a phone number for questions.
questions.explanation: Iris 提议附上供提问的电话号码。

questions.prompt: How much time remains before the event?
questions.evidence: We have three days, so it is not an emergency.
questions.explanation: Iris 说明还剩三天，所以并非紧急事件。

questions.prompt: When should they update the poster?
questions.evidence: We should still update the poster today.
questions.explanation: 虽然不紧急，仍应今天更新海报。

questions.prompt: What will they discuss after people arrive?
options: The price of a train ticket.
questions.evidence: After people arrive, we can discuss their ideas for the next event.
questions.explanation: 大家到场后会讨论下一次活动的想法。

instructions: Listen to the conversation before reading the transcript and answer independently. After submitting, check the transcript and reasons for any errors.
transcript:
Iris: I saw your message about the community conversation on Saturday. Did you mean ten in the morning?
Paul: I meant two in the afternoon. I should have written the time clearly. I apologize for the confusion.
Iris: Thanks for explaining. The poster says “Saturday” but does not mention a time. We should clarify it before we print more copies.
Paul: I agree. Could you tell me whether the hall is free at two? I have not received a response from the manager yet.
Iris: I can ask her now. Our purpose is to make sure people have the right information, not to blame anyone.
Paul: Good. The dialogue will be informal, and everyone can share an opinion about neighborhood activities.
Iris: The manager says the hall is free at two. She asks us to remind her on Friday.
Paul: I will reply to her message. Could you repeat which door people should use?
Iris: The side door. The main door is being repaired. Please describe that on the poster in one short sentence.
Paul: How about the phrase “Please enter through the side door”?
Iris: That sounds polite and easy to understand. We can also include a phone number for questions.
Iris: I suggest we explain the reason for the change in a short, clear message, rather than a formal letter.
Paul: Is the change urgent? I do not want our tone to make people upset.
Iris: We have three days, so it is not an emergency. We should still update the poster today.
Paul: I will listen to your suggestion and check the time once more. Then I will send you the final version.
Iris: Thank you. This exchange has helped us communicate the plan clearly. After people arrive, we can discuss their ideas for the next event.
